content: NOL1, also known as putative ribosomal RNA methyltransferase NOP2, is an enzyme in humans encoded by the NOP2 gene. The protein produced by this gene functions as a nucleolar antigen and is specifically expressed in proliferating cells. It is absent in non-proliferating normal tissues but is detectable in various human tumors. Overexpression of the p120 protein, which is encoded by this gene, induces malignant transformation in 3T3 cells. Conversely, when antisense p120 mRNA is introduced, the transformed cells revert to their original, non-malignant phenotype. This indicates a critical role of p120 in cellular transformation and malignancy. The expression of the p120 protein significantly increases during the G1/S transition of the cell cycle. This observation suggests that p120 plays a regulatory role in the cell cycle and nucleolar activity, both of which are essential for cell proliferation. Additionally, NOL1 has been demonstrated to interact with MCRS1, further implicating its involvement in cellular processes related to growth and proliferation.
